The analysis suggests that while AI investment continues, higher borrowing costs and slowing earnings growth could pressure firms to justify their spending on infrastructure.
items.title: Jefferies warns rising borrowing costs threaten global AI expansion

items.summary: Morgan Stanley reports that rapid AI infrastructure investment may outpace electricity availability, creating a power shortfall for US data centers. The firm estimates a 32-gigawatt deficit by 2028, potentially squeezing out smaller competitors. While major tech firms could capture most capacity additions, the lack of power and suitable land may constrain chip deployment and slow the AI boom.
items.title: Morgan Stanley Warns AI Power Shortfall Risks Outpacing Chip Supply

items.summary: US President Donald Trump waived punitive tariffs on countries buying Russian oil, offering India relief from potential 100% duties on US exports. However, experts warn Washington retains the option to revive penalties as leverage in trade negotiations. While India prioritizes energy security, the waiver provides no lasting certainty, leaving New Delhi exposed to renewed US pressure unless it demonstrates that coercion carries a cost.
items.title: Trump Waives Russian Oil Tariffs for India Amid Uncertainty

items.summary: Croatian President Zoran Milanovic met with visiting Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi in Zagreb on October 16, 2026. During the discussion, Milanovic expressed Croatia's willingness to strengthen exchanges and advance mutually beneficial cooperation with China, reaffirming Croatia's commitment to the one-China policy. Wang Yi conveyed greetings from President Xi Jinping and highlighted China's commitment to peaceful development and mutual benefits. The two sides also discussed China-Europe relations, with Wang noting the absence of fundamental conflicts of interest between China and the EU. Milanovic, as an EU member, emphasized maintaining Croatia's independence while adhering to the bloc's common foreign and security policy.
items.title: Croatian President Meets Chinese Foreign Minister to Strengthen Bilateral Cooperation

items.summary: Chinese Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang addressed the 2026 World Vocational and Technical Education Development Conference in Tianjin, calling for strengthened international cooperation in vocational education. He emphasized enhancing policy communication, aligning rules, and promoting cross-border skills allocation. Ding highlighted China's role in global skills training and the need to integrate new technologies into vocational education to meet economic demands.
items.title: Chinese Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang Urges Global Vocational Education Cooperation

items.summary: Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned that Donald Trump's decision to pause sanctions on Russia would intensify the war in Ukraine. He stated that lifting pressure and providing financial rewards encourages Vladimir Putin to continue attacks. This follows a massive Russian strike on Ukraine's energy infrastructure, which Zelenskyy described as one of the worst yet. Zelenskyy called for Europe to negotiate directly with Moscow and urged the US to resurrect the Lindsey Graham sanctions bill. Meanwhile, Trump announced a hold on new sanctions and a deal to purchase Russian diesel, actions Zelenskyy criticized as ignoring the law meant to pressure Russia.
items.title: Zelenskyy Warns Trump Sanctions Lift Will Intensify Ukraine War

items.summary: Former Punjab Chief Minister Sukhbir Badal directly blamed current Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann for the murder of anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh Jhota. Speaking at the SAD office in Chandigarh, Badal accused the AAP-led government of failing to curb drug trafficking and maintain law and order. Badal's wife, Harsimrat Kaur Badal, joined the criticism, alleging a nexus between traffickers and officials and demanding the government's dismissal. The family and protesters are demanding a CBI probe and Mann's resignation.
items.title: Sukhbir Badal Blames Bhagwant Mann for Parvinder Jhota's Murder

items.summary: The India Meteorological Department issued orange alerts for five Kerala districts and yellow alerts for nine others due to heavy rainfall and thunderstorms. The Kerala State Disaster Management Authority urged residents in vulnerable areas to relocate to safer places and avoid water bodies. District control rooms remain operational round the clock, and toll-free numbers are available for assistance.
items.title: Kerala districts under orange and yellow rain alerts

items.summary: A political confrontation in Delhi involves allegations of vote theft and calls for regime change. Janata Party founder Abhijeet Dipke secured conditional bail after signing a 50,000 rupee peace bond, while associates remain jailed. The Congress party received approval to hold a rally at Ramlila Maidan on 1 November. Meanwhile, the opposition challenges Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar in the Supreme Court regarding voter list revisions. Union ministers accuse the opposition of destabilizing the government through street violence, which the Congress denies. The India Today Group also launched an AI-powered Ramayana micro-drama series on its platform Life Tak.
items.title: Political Showdown in Delhi Over Election Commissioner and Vote Theft Allegations

items.summary: Actor Imran Khan Pal filed a petition in the Bombay High Court to challenge a 'leave India' notice issued by the Foreigners Regional Registration Officer. Khan argues the notice is arbitrary, unreasoned, and violates his fundamental rights under Articles 14 and 21 of the Indian Constitution. He claims the action was punitive and aimed at stifling dissent without due process or a hearing. The petition seeks urgent intervention to stay the notice.
items.title: Actor Imran Khan Challenges 'Leave India' Notice in Bombay High Court

items.summary: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India issued an improvement notice to AB Hotels Limited, operator of the Radisson Blu Hotel in New Delhi, citing food safety lapses. Inspections revealed pest infestations, equipment failures, and improper food handling. Notably, cooking oils with TPC values of 31 and 24.4 were found, exceeding the permitted 25% limit. The regulator directed immediate corrective measures and threatened licence suspension for non-compliance.
items.title: FSSAI Issues Improvement Notice to Radisson Blu Delhi Over Food Safety Violations

items.summary: CNA reported that most haze shelters across Singapore remained empty or locked on Saturday, despite high heat and pollution. While few residents utilized the facilities, those who did, such as retirees Ms Poh and Mr Low, welcomed the air-conditioned respite. Ms Florence Ong also appreciated the free facility, noting it offered relief without needing to run home air-conditioners. The government had recently stepped up measures after PM2.5 readings hit very high levels.
items.title: Few Singaporeans Use Haze Shelters Despite Heat and Pollution

items.summary: A Supreme Court-appointed five-member committee launched a portal to receive complaints regarding violence at Jantar Mantar and other Delhi locations during July 2026. The Union Home Ministry stated the committee will prioritize cases involving pellet guns, harassment of female protesters, and excessive force. Submissions can be made online, in person, or via email to ensure witness protection.
items.title: SC Panel Launches Portal for July Violence Complaints

items.summary: Chilean-American author Isabel Allende won Spain's €1m Premio Planeta literary prize under the pseudonym Luz Ventura. The award, the 75th edition, recognized her sequel to The House of the Spirits, titled La hora antes del alba. Speaking at the ceremony in Barcelona, Allende compared the win to receiving the Nobel Prize. She noted that while the prize is lucrative, it is not the most prestigious in the Spanish-speaking world. The article highlights the prize's history of favoring established writers and mentions a previous instance where a pseudonym was used to conceal three male authors. Allende, 84, stated she entered to avoid the embarrassment of coming last.
items.title: Isabel Allende Wins Spanish Literary Prize Under Pseudonym

items.summary: DMK leader M K Stalin labeled the ruling TVK a "Breaking Bad Party" following the arrest of functionary Boopalan, who officials say concealed 135 kg of methamphetamine. Stalin, citing preliminary investigations, urged authorities to identify others in the alleged narcotics network and dismantle it, questioning how a party member could be involved in such a large-scale operation while publicly advocating against drugs.
items.title: Stalin Calls TVK a Breaking Bad Party After Meth Seizure

items.summary: Sebastian Rucci, a developer with a controversial past, sought to build California's largest AI datacenter in Imperial County, aiming to house Google's AI training. Despite securing interest from Google and promising jobs and tax revenue, the project faced intense local opposition. Residents cited concerns over water scarcity, environmental damage, and noise. Following a judge's ruling requiring an extensive environmental review, construction is paused. Rucci plans to challenge the decision, while the community continues to fight the development.
items.title: Developer's AI Datacenter Project Halted by Community Resistance and Legal Challenges

items.summary: Wasted energy from 50 million electric motors in U.S. factories and buildings could free gigawatts of grid power. Currently, only 16% of industrial and 4% of commercial motors use variable frequency drives (VFDs) to optimize efficiency. Experts argue that wider adoption could supply power for five years of data center growth without new generation. Manufacturers and advocates urge federal agencies and utilities to offer incentives and standards to accelerate rollout, citing rising electricity costs and grid stress as key drivers.
items.title: Wasted Motor Energy Offers Grid Relief Through Variable Frequency Drives

items.summary: ZDNET reports that ten states have legalized plug-in solar systems, allowing residents to install backyard solar setups. While Utah was the first, nine others have followed. Approximately 24 additional states are working on legislation, with some bills advancing in Massachusetts and New York. However, plug-in solar remains illegal in several states due to safety concerns and utility regulations.
items.title: Ten States Legalize Plug-in Solar Systems While Others Advance Legislation

items.summary: Historical ship fires linked to untreated fishmeal led to the adoption of ethoxyquin as a fire retardant in animal feed. While effective in preventing spontaneous combustion, ethoxyquin is now recognized as a carcinogen. Consequently, the European Union and several other nations have banned or restricted its use in animal feed. Despite these restrictions, the chemical remains permitted in the U.S., Australia, Japan, and South Korea. The aquaculture industry continues to face challenges regarding chemical safety and consumer perception, with some companies shifting to alternatives like rosemary extract or vitamin E.
items.title: Ethoxyquin: From Fire Retardant to Controversial Feed Additive

items.summary: A report by Action Against Hunger identifies Pakistan and Bangladesh among the ten nations facing the world's most severe food crises. The study estimates 10.6 million people in Pakistan will need aid in 2026. Globally, 177 million people live in these ten countries, where acute hunger affects 266 million across 47 nations. Pakistan ranked 106th in the 2026 Global Hunger Index with a score of 25.5, categorized as 'serious'. Factors include poverty, climate disasters, and economic instability.
items.title: Pakistan and Bangladesh Rank Among Worst Hunger Nations

items.summary: Pope Leo XIV is set to be discharged from Rome's Gemelli Hospital on Saturday, four days after surgery to remove a lung cancerous growth. The Vatican confirmed he will celebrate Mass and give the Angelus prayer in St Peter's Square on Sunday. Further tests regarding cancer spread are pending, and his fitness for a planned trip to Peru remains unclear.
items.title: Pope Leo XIV Discharged After Lung Cancer Surgery

items.summary: Frontline health workers in Beni, Democratic Republic of Congo, received the Ervebo vaccine on Friday. Health authorities suggest it may offer protection against the related Bundibugyo virus, though efficacy is still being studied. The vaccine is used under a compassionate-use programme. As of Wednesday, the Health Ministry reported 9,066 confirmed cases and 4,381 deaths. The World Health Organization states the outbreak remains out of control.
items.title: Frontline workers in DRC receive Ervebo vaccine amid growing Ebola outbreak

items.summary: Andrew Bailey, the Bank of England governor, participated in a walkout by finance leaders at an IMF meeting in Bangkok. The group departed in protest after Russian finance minister Anton Siluanov addressed them in Russian. Joachim Nagel of the German Bundesbank noted that nearly half the delegates left. European diplomats stated the Ukraine war is existential for Europe and that normalizing relations with Russia is impossible.
items.title: Bank of England Governor Joins IMF Walkout Over Russia

items.summary: A Chinese nursery owner and five staff members were jailed after poisoning over 200 children with lead-tainted food. Li Huifang received a life sentence, while others faced prison terms and fines. Investigations revealed inedible paint was used to enhance meals, resulting in lead levels 2,000 times the safety limit. Dozens of officials were later found attempting to cover up the incident.
items.title: Chinese Nursery Owner Jailed for Life Over Lead Poisoning

items.summary: A Delhi court ordered the release of Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke on Saturday, a day after his preventive arrest. Police cited traffic concerns and prior violations as reasons for the initial detention. Dipke was released from Mandir Marg police station. Meanwhile, student leader Neha Bora was also released. The arrests occurred amidst protests demanding the resignation of Election Commission chief Kumar over concerns regarding electoral roll revisions.
items.title: Delhi Court Orders Release of Abhijeet Dipke Following Preventive Arrest

items.summary: Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar stated that Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is unlikely to visit Budapest later this month despite an invitation for the 70th anniversary of the 1956 Hungarian Revolution. Magyar expressed this view in an interview with 444.hu, noting that attendance was improbable even though Russian President Vladimir Putin was not invited. The two leaders previously agreed to meet again later this year at the EU summit in Brussels.
items.title: Hungarian PM Says Zelenskyy Unlikely to Visit Budapest

items.summary: Rolls-Royce is expanding its Goodwood factory with a £300m investment from owner BMW to meet growing demand for highly customised vehicles. The company reports that the average buyer is now 43, down from 56 in 2010, driven by younger, tech-rich clients. Bespoke requests range from interior feathers to dog portraits, with prices reaching seven-figure sums. While production output peaked at 6,032 cars, recent deliveries have fallen. The expansion aims to handle complex commissions rather than increase volume, as the brand navigates challenges like Chinese market slowdowns and a shift in electric vehicle strategy.
items.title: Rolls-Royce Expands Goodwood Factory Amid Custom Craze

items.summary: A list of six new fiction novels is presented, with all information sourced from publishers. The titles include 'Exit Party' by Emily St John Mandel, set in 2031; 'Partita' by Barbara Kingsolver; 'All Our Noble Selves' by Kate Atkinson, set in 1951; 'Victorious' by VE Schwab; 'The Need' by Megan Mostyn Brown; and 'Fair Ones' by Lydia Millet. Brief synopses describe the plots, characters, and settings of each book, ranging from dystopian futures and historical mysteries to supernatural thrillers and family dramas. Specific details, such as character ages and historical dates, are included within the descriptions.
items.title: Six New Novels by Barbara Kingsolver, Kate Atkinson, and Others

items.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that Russia is intensifying attacks on energy infrastructure to cause a blackout before winter. He claimed over 15 critical facilities were targeted and that Moscow aims to leave millions without power. While the Russian Defense Ministry confirmed strikes on specific sites, Zelenskyy also criticized a US sanctions waiver, arguing it encourages further aggression.
items.title: Zelenskyy Accuses Russia of Planned Winter Blackout in Ukraine

items.summary: Senior Labour figures are increasingly worried about the dangers of artificial intelligence, fearing the technology could fall into the hands of bad actors or be used to create bioweapons. While some, like Ed Miliband, warn of threats to humanity, others, such as Prof Elena Simperl, argue that immediate risks like hacking and addiction are more credible than existential threats. The government is currently balancing the need for safety regulations with the desire to avoid falling behind in productivity. Recent warnings from security services and a shift in government posture under Andy Burnham have intensified the focus on AI security and international cooperation.
items.title: Senior Labour Figures Express Deep Concerns Over AI Risks and Safety

items.summary: A doctor at YCM Hospital in Pimpri-Chinchwad was suspended after a viral video allegedly showed a liquor party inside the post-mortem room. PCMC officials ordered an inquiry following the incident involving Dr Vaibhav Avinash Mhaske, who was found intoxicated. Additional Commissioner Kuldeep Jangam issued notices for written explanations, while Municipal Commissioner Vijay Suryavanshi ordered immediate suspension. A departmental inquiry is underway, with a chargesheet anticipated within 15 days.
items.title: Doctor Suspended After Viral Video Shows Liquor in Mortuary

items.summary: Mahela Jayawardene has ended his second stint as head coach of Mumbai Indians, with the franchise confirming his departure. Owner Nita Ambani praised his leadership and contribution, while Jayawardene expressed gratitude for his time with the team. The franchise must now find a new head coach before the November 15 IPL retention deadline.
items.title: Mahela Jayawardene Steps Down as Mumbai Indians Head Coach

items.summary: Abhijeet Dipke, founder of the Cockroach Janta Party, was granted conditional bail by a Special Executive Magistrate court following his detention ahead of a proposed 'Lehra Do Tiranga' march in Delhi. He signed a personal bond of Rs 50,000 and was released immediately. Dipke was arrested under Sections 126 and 170 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita for breach of peace. Other CJP leaders and AISA president Neha Bora were also detained and released after furnishing bonds.
items.title: CJP Founder Abhijeet Dipke Granted Conditional Bail After Detention

items.summary: Decades after apartheid, South Africans are pursuing legal action for past crimes, focusing on the 1960 Sharpeville massacre where police killed at least 69 protesters. Paulina Mathinye, a survivor's descendant, joined a potential class action lawsuit to challenge the Indemnity Act 61 of 1961, which blocks legal redress. The case aims to secure reparations and recognition. Similar efforts include court rulings on the deaths of Chief Albert Luthuli and the Cradock Four, and a reopened inquiry into Steve Biko's death. A formal inquiry is also investigating whether apartheid-era prosecution recommendations were deliberately shelved. These legal moves represent a new wave of efforts to confront historical injustice.
items.title: South Africans Seek Justice for Apartheid-Era Crimes

items.summary: ixigo reported a net profit of Rs 63 crore for Q2 FY27, marking a turnaround from a Rs 3.46 crore loss the prior year. Hotels emerged as the fastest-growing segment with a gross transaction value of Rs 111.34 crore, up 159% year-on-year. Revenue from operations rose to Rs 320.96 crore, supported by a partial stake sale in Freshbus.
items.title: ixigo Reports Q2 Profit Driven by Hotel Booking Growth

items.summary: ICICI Bank reported a 17.7% year-on-year increase in net interest income to Rs 25,339 crore in the second quarter of FY27. The lender's net interest margin stood at 4.18%, while gross non-performing assets declined to 1.20%. Total period-end deposits grew 27.1% to Rs 20.49 lakh crore, and total assets rose 22.6% to Rs 32.93 lakh crore as of September 30, 2026, according to a regulatory filing.
items.title: ICICI Bank Reports Strong Q2 Profit and Asset Growth

items.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps stated that a super tanker caught fire after striking a sea mine in the Strait of Hormuz. The IRGC navy accused the vessel of turning off its systems to evade detection while attempting to use an unauthorized route. The US military disputes IRGC control of the strait, asserting it remains open for business.
items.title: IRGC Accuses Tanker of Evading Detection After Mine Strike in Strait of Hormuz

items.summary: The article suggests that book covers often influence selection decisions before a reader can assess the content. To address this, the free app Uncovered.ink is recommended as an alternative to Kindle. This tool allows users to preview the opening chapter of a book directly, bypassing visual marketing and helping readers discover new titles based on the actual text rather than superficial design elements.
items.title: Uncovered.ink Helps Readers Find Books Without Cover Art

items.summary: Europe's solar and storage industry reached nearly one million jobs in 2025, yet Women in Solar+ Europe highlights a retention crisis. While purpose drives recruitment, women leave due to workplace experiences, lack of career progression, and the 'motherhood penalty.' Surveys of 22 European countries indicate nearly four in ten respondents may seek new roles within a year. Experts argue that inspiration alone is insufficient; organizations must implement transparent promotion criteria, flexible policies, and strong leadership to retain talent. The industry faces a competitiveness issue if it fails to support the women who have already committed to the energy transition.
items.title: Solar Industry Faces Retention Challenges Despite Strong Recruitment

items.summary: Groundwater cleanup at the Escambia Wood Treating Company site in Pensacola, Florida, nicknamed Mount Dioxin, is set to begin this fall. The EPA and Escambia County have hired a contractor to treat the contamination, a project estimated to take three to five years. This cleanup follows the 2010 completion of soil remediation and the 1997 relocation of approximately 400 households from the area. The site, originally designated a Superfund site in 1989, remains vacant while awaiting a paying tenant. Future reviews are scheduled for fall 2027.
items.title: Groundwater Cleanup Begins at Florida Superfund Site Decades Later

items.summary: The French government announced measures to accelerate electrification and improve electricity demand flexibility. It plans to exempt solar-plus-storage projects up to 25 MW from current connection limits by the end of 2026, provided grid injection remains under 17 MW. The government also intends to make heat pump subsidies conditional on smart controls from 2027 and encourage smart meter integration. Industry players like Gimelec, EDF, Neoen, and NW Group have committed to expanding flexibility capacity and deploying remote-control systems by 2030, aiming to mobilize gigawatts of capacity and save households money through optimized energy consumption.
items.title: France Eases Grid Rules for Solar-Plus-Storage Projects

items.summary: Hundreds gathered in Melbourne to honor Jayda Allen Bonner, a 21-year-old Indigenous woman killed in an inner-suburban apartment. Her mother and aunt called for action against violence against women. A 31-year-old man was charged with murder. Police investigations continue, with the Homicide Squad examining interactions between police and the victim. Family supporters marched to Parliament demanding domestic violence reforms.
items.title: Hundreds mourn Indigenous woman killed in Melbourne apartment

items.summary: This article presents ten facts regarding the origins of Halloween, tracing the holiday from ancient Celtic rituals to modern American customs. It clarifies that Halloween descends from the Celtic festival of Samhain, which marked the end of harvest and the start of winter roughly 2,000 years ago. The text explains that while Christian holy days and later marketing layers were added, the core seasonal frame remained. Specific traditions like jack-o'-lanterns originated from Irish turnip carvings rather than American pumpkins, and trick-or-treating merged medieval souling with Scottish guising and American pranking in the 1920s and 1930s. The article also notes that associations with Satanism are modern constructs and that the holiday's current candy-centric nature emerged only after World War II.
items.title: Article Debunks Common Halloween Myths and Traces Origins

items.summary: Police in Sydney's Northern Beaches have arrested a 13-year-old boy following multiple reports of alleged sexual touching of women on walking trails around Narrabeen Lagoon. The incidents, occurring between October 1 and 12, involved a man allegedly approaching victims on an e-bike. Superintendent John Duncan stated that police have increased surveillance and patrols while encouraging the public to come forward with information.
items.title: Police Arrest Teenager in Sexual Touching Probe at Narrabeen Lagoon

items.summary: Hundreds of former fighters in Ethiopia's Tigray region have registered for a reintegration program to return to civilian life. They gathered at the Tigray Martyrs' Memorial Monument in Mekelle, two weeks after federal forces recaptured the city. This follows renewed fighting that shattered the 2022 peace agreement. A new caretaker administration has been announced to restore services and prepare for elections.
items.title: Former Tigray Fighters Register for Reintegration Program

items.summary: Japanese Minister Yasuhiro Hanashi announced a government initiative to raise youth awareness regarding the Northern Territories dispute. The plan involves organizing school trips near the islands and sharing information on social media. Hanashi also emphasized promoting the issue abroad and resuming bilateral exchange programs. He described the dispute as the biggest pending issue between Japan and Russia, stating that resolving it is essential for the entire nation.
items.title: Japan Minister Plans Youth Awareness Campaign on Northern Territories Dispute

items.summary: This article presents 15 facts detailing the origins and evolution of Halloween traditions in the United States. It explains that the jack-o'-lantern began as a carved turnip in Ireland and Scotland before pumpkins replaced them due to availability in North America. The text notes that trick-or-treating is a relatively recent custom, emerging in the 1930s and gaining popularity after World War II. Candy corn, originally sold as chicken feed in the 1880s, later became associated with the holiday. The article also covers the history of UNICEF's fundraising campaign, which started in 1950, and discusses the agricultural and retail aspects of pumpkin production and candy sales. It addresses common myths, such as the rarity of a full moon on Halloween and the lack of evidence for poisoned candy scares, attributing the latter to a single family crime in 1974 that fueled broader fears. The piece concludes by comparing Halloween to similar celebrations in other countries and noting its significant impact on the retail calendar.
items.title: Article details 15 facts explaining Halloween traditions and origins

items.summary: Rahul Anand, an IMF official, welcomed Japan's plan to temporarily lower the consumption tax on food to 1% from 8% to address soaring prices. While supporting the targeted, budget-neutral approach, Anand warned against fiscal deterioration given Japan's exceptionally high debt level. He also noted concerns regarding rising long-term interest rates and the need to build buffers while maintaining a downward trend in the debt-to-GDP ratio.
items.title: IMF Official Welcomes Japan's Temporary Tax Cut Plan Amid High Debt Concerns

items.summary: Under-30s describe a bleak lack of nightlife, citing the disappearance of traditional nightclubs in towns like Woking and Tonbridge. The Night Time Industries Association states a quarter of UK towns have lost all nightclubs. Factors include the cost of living crisis and a cultural shift toward sober socialising. Some young people are creating their own events to fill the gap.
items.title: Young people report loss of nightlife venues in UK towns

items.summary: Multilateral development banks published a framework on Saturday to strengthen support for mineral-rich developing economies. The initiative moves beyond extraction to promote processing, refining, and manufacturing. Banks like the World Bank and Asian Development Bank will coordinate financing and infrastructure to boost domestic value addition and attract private investment.
items.title: MDBs Outline Framework to Boost Critical Minerals Processing in Developing Economies

items.summary: Billy Childish, a 66-year-old British punk icon known as Steve Hamper, rejects the commercialization of art, stating that 'Professional art kills art.' He has released over 100 albums and created thousands of paintings since the 1970s. Childish, who grew up in Chatham, works across punk, garage, and folk styles with bands like Thee Headcoats. He refuses to sign contracts, citing a desire for creative freedom. His recent biography by Ted Kessler highlights his authentic, DIY approach. Childish continues to perform and create, emphasizing instinct and personal expression over market demands.
items.title: Billy Childish Rejects Commercial Art in Punk Legacy

items.summary: Thomas Piketty and 44 co-authors from the Global Justice Project propose a future where global wealth shifts from the top 0.001% to the poorest 50%, driven by climate action and sufficiency. While acknowledging the path is politically difficult, Piketty argues that current inequality and climate change create a dystopian alternative. He suggests that without democratic deliberation on issues like shorter working hours and reduced consumption, society risks collapse. The proposal emphasizes international cooperation to avoid resource conflicts and ensure shared prosperity.
items.title: Thomas Piketty Warns of Dystopian Future Prepared by Billionaires

items.summary: Indian Captain Smit Machchhar recounted a harrowing ordeal aboard a flydubai flight in September, where he was allegedly attacked by his Omani co-pilot, Hamam al-Hammami. Machchhar stated he realized he had to act to survive, eventually opening the cockpit door for passengers to intervene. The aircraft diverted to Tabuk after a sharp altitude drop, landing safely.
items.title: Indian Pilot Recalls Near-Death Cockpit Assault Experience

items.summary: Lawyer Ratul Bora plans to challenge two bail orders granted by the Gauhati High Court in the Zubeen Garg death case. Bora alleges loopholes in the charge sheet are weakening the prosecution. While the Singapore Police concluded Garg drowned due to intoxication, Assam authorities maintain it was murder. Bora seeks Supreme Court intervention to prevent further bail grants for the remaining accused.
items.title: Lawyer Challenges Bail Orders in Zubeen Garg Death Case at Supreme Court

items.summary: Portugal is hosting major demonstrations as part of a wider European cost-of-living crisis. Housing rights movements and trade unions affiliated with the CGTP union federation are rallying in Porto, Coimbra, and Lisbon. Protesters cite rising prices, fuel costs, and housing shortages as drivers. While organizers emphasize peaceful assembly, French demonstrations turned violent. Authorities urge protests remain lawful.
items.title: Portugal Joins European Cost-of-Living Protests Amid Housing Crisis

items.summary: Tamil Nadu aims to recover from a disappointing start to their Ranji Trophy campaign with a home match against Uttarakhand at Chepauk in Chennai. Following a loss to Rajasthan where they scored 274 all out after reaching 203 for four, the team utilized time in Chennai to bond and prepare. Coach Yo Mahesh highlighted positives, including a promising bowling unit where debutant Deepesh Devendran took three wickets.
